name: Oyster Plant
description: Oyster Plant (Tradescantia spathacea), also known as Moses-in-the-Cradle, is a houseplant with vivid purple and green leaves. The ASPCA lists Tradescantia as toxic to cats, with dermatitis (skin irritation) as the documented clinical sign. Its sap acts as a contact irritant. If a broken leaf oozes sap onto a cat's skin or fur, it can cause localized redness, itching, or a rash. Chewing the plant may also cause mild mouth or stomach upset in some cats, though skin irritation from sap contact is the harm confirmed by authorities. Because of its colorful leaves, the oyster plant can attract curious cats. It is best to keep it out of reach. If your cat gets sap on its skin, wash the area gently with water to prevent a rash. Contact a veterinarian if your cat eats the plant and any drooling or stomach upset does not improve.
safetyNotes: Toxic principle: the sap contains an unidentified irritant; the ASPCA does not list calcium oxalate for this plant
Mechanism: sap contact causes contact dermatitis (skin irritation), the clinical sign documented by the ASPCA
Symptoms: skin or eye contact with sap may cause redness, irritation, or rash; some cats may also drool or vomit after chewing the plant
The ornamental purple-and-green leaves make this a popular houseplant — keep it out of cat reach
Symptoms are usually mild; rinse any sap off skin with water and consult your vet if GI symptoms persist
